en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Dukatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (3) 15.25.
The "Root-with-root" Dyads, etc., and the "Wholesome" Triads.

A wholesome state that is both a root (hetu) and accompanied by roots (sahetuka) is a condition, by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya), for a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by roots and is not wholesome.

A wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by roots and is not wholesome. [A wholesome state] that is both a root and accompanied by roots...

And a wholesome state that possesses a cause but is not itself a cause is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither-rooted nor has a root, which is neither-wholesome nor has a root, and for a state that is neither-wholesome nor has a root and does not possess a cause.
A wholesome state that possesses a cause but is not itself a cause is [a condition] for a state that is neither-rooted nor has a root and is neither-wholesome... [and so forth].

A state that is accompanied by a root and is not itself a root (sahetuko ceva na ca hetu) and is wholesome (kusala) is related to a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root (nahetussa ceva naahetukassa) and is unwholesome (nakusala) by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya).

A state that is accompanied by a root and is not itself a root and is wholesome is related to a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root and is both unwholesome and neither-root-nor-accompanied-by-root... by way of object-condition.

And [factors] that are both roots and associated with roots, as well as wholesome factors that are neither roots nor associated with roots, are conditions by way of object-condition for a factor that is neither a root nor associated with a root and is unwholesome.

Factors that are both roots and associated with roots, as well as wholesome factors that are both roots and associated with roots, and factors that are neither roots nor associated with roots and are wholesome, are conditions by way of object-condition for a factor that is neither a root nor associated with a root and is unwholesome. [Factors] that are both roots and associated with roots...
Wholesome states that are both skillful and with-root, as well as wholesome states that are neither root nor with-root,
are related to a state that is neither root nor with-root and is not wholesome by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*). Wholesome states that are both roots and with-root,
as well as wholesome states that are neither root nor with-root, are related to a state that is neither root nor with-root and is neither wholesome nor with-root.
And [this] is a condition for a state that is neither-root nor accompanied by root and is unwholesome, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*).

There are nine [answers] for object, nine for predominance (*adhipati*), proximity (*anantara*), contiguity (*samanantara*), decisive support (*upanissaya*), absence (*natthi*), and disappearance (*vigata*).

A unwholesome state that is both root and accompanied by root is a condition for a state that is neither-root nor accompanied by root and is not unwholesome, by way of object-condition. (By this method, nine questions are to be formulated.)
In the object condition, there are nine; in the proximity, contiguity, decisive support, absence, and disappearance conditions, there are nine.

An indeterminate state that is both a root-cause and accompanied by a root-cause is a condition, by way of the object condition, for a state that is neither a root-cause nor accompanied by a root-cause and is not indeterminate. (Nine questions are to be formulated.
In the object, predominance, and decisive support conditions, there are nine.
